Data handling
One incomplete trailing fragment is rejected. Unknown response sizes remain unknown. Duplicate requests are preserved.
SHA-256 · original gzip

The browser reads a compact, lossless preparation of all valid requests. Deterministic hash inputs are prepared once for speed; Bloom, FM, DGIM and exact checks execute incrementally in a Web Worker. The download includes the untouched source file and the preparation script.

A QUICK FIELD GUIDE

A stream is a sequence.
A sketch is a memory.

This lab replays genuine requests from a historical NASA web server log. It is not connected to today's NASA traffic.

  1. Press Start, or take one Step.

    Every event updates all three algorithms and their exact baselines. Use one request per second to watch individual decisions.

  2. Open the Algorithm lab.

    Inspect real bit positions, maximum-zero registers and DGIM buckets. Change a parameter to restart with a different memory–accuracy trade-off.

  3. Compare with the truth.

    Approximation is visible, not hidden. FM's teaching estimator can have very large errors. Bloom has false positives; DGIM approximates the oldest bucket.

Memory labels in the live lab show logical payload, excluding JavaScript overhead and input caches. The Experiments page shows measured Python state and recorded benchmarks.

Mobile tip: use the menu at the top left to switch views. All controls work by touch and keyboard.
